cohort: Nine pregnant patients with Congenital Myasthenic Syndromes (CMS) and a history of pregnancy, totaling sixteen pregnancies, were followed in two tertiary hospitals.
finding: Most pregnancies in women with CMS, managed by a multidisciplinary team, did not result in major complications for mothers or newborns, though one woman with a CHAT mutation experienced significant symptom worsening during pregnancy and post-partum.
